digest.component_or_area: plan-review attestation and clarity rule framework
propositions: Proposed deterministic criteria for plan clarity (required sections, placeholder detection, per-AC proof markers, edit-set grounding, conjunction hygiene, Testing heading shape) when applied to 574 closed tickets with signed attestation, generate false positives on valid accepted work

Six specific historical counterexamples (tickets 003d, 03c6, 0730, 090f, 35bc) demonstrate that section headings are coaching conventions not oracles, semantic content aliases are valid, conditional scoped work is executable without proof sentinels, read-only analysis has no repository edit-set, conjunctions can express atomic cross-surface invariants, and mechanical migrations do not require negative user-flow scenarios

Deterministic hard-failure rules for section presence, placeholder lexicon, per-AC proof coverage markers, file_impact requirements, AC conjunction counts, and Testing section structure fail corpus validation and should be narrowed to advisory-only or semantic applicability gates rather than blocking validity verdicts

Reliability improvement requires explicit applicability scoping (semantic section alias normalization, read-only work exemptions, new user-facing behavior gates) and evidence-bearing signal downgrade (placeholder and conjunction hygiene remain useful review prompts but cannot serve as validity criteria)
The audit corpus of 574 signed and closed tickets with plan-review PASS and completion-verifier PASS provides sufficient counterexample density to reject each proposed hard criterion as written
